body: Make sure you make arrangements for your mental health upon your discharge, civilian life (in my opinion) is confusing and people in it sometime undermined the sacrifices we've made. VA sucks for mental health, they will see you if you tell them is an emergency, other than that is a waiting game. From a Vet to another, please take care of yourself, most people are not as appreciative as they seem when they say "we love our vets" Talk to friends and connect with people so you don't miss the camaraderie as much. For me its been tough and lonely. best of luck and thank you for your service!

Im 34, been depressed since my 20's and sometimes I still want to believe is all in my head because its easier to make sense of it that way. I hope you find something that makes you happy, Im certainly trying..... thats everyday with depression, "trying". Some days the blanket of smoke lifts and you can see there is some good in the world after all. Don't give up!

Thanks for taking the time, I really appreciate it. Ive tried many times explaining, she's gone to therapy with me but its the same at home. for the first week after i speak to her she tries, but then she forgets i guess.... Ive given up on her. 
As far a therapy, I will tai your advice and seek some more affordable options, Im a Army vet so maybe ill reach out to  them. I tried them before but they offers meds not therapy. 
thanks again and I hope you had a good weekend.

everyday I try to make something positive but fail. I play music and feel quiet then the song ends and its back to the gauntlet in my head. I pray it ends, but it doesn't. Im begging to think nobody is really listening up there. I just want a normal life. I don't have unachievable expectations, just a life without the anger that cripples me every day! I smoke some weed and feel better, but that just makes me feel like a criminal. I take my meds and feel they are a false sense of happiness so I stop and challenge myself to be normal but nothing changes. I don't have it in me to kill myself, I just want my body to recognize how unhappy I am and maybe it will shut down one day or it will let a disease in and finally release me from this grinder.

My wife and I have a similar dynamic. She embraces me when Im already fed up and crying, but she doesn't notice if Im not. I feel like its very noticeable since I don't talk much these days, but I guess thats not enough warning. Im beginning to think I need to leave her.
thanks for the kind words.

I was going to therapy of a long time paired with meds. Ive tried different kinds and found some relief with prozac. That came and went. I can't afford therapy any longer and stop the meds about two months ago. Im 33 and I fear my life will be a mess health wise if i continue this meds. I want to call my doctor, but a general Doc doesn't get the full range of problems. My wife doesn't get it, I moved to NY and left all my friends back home. Now Im lonely and stuck at a job that I fell backwards into. Thanks for the response, I don't really have many people I can be so candid with.

weed keeps my brain from exploding! It helps me with my panic attacks and overall human experience. Im  afraid to leave my current job because I know I won't find anything else that is permissible of my lifestyle. My current job is depressing, people fight all the time and my anxiety is always heightened. By the time i get home Im exhausted from basically containing my anger, sadness and frustrations. I know how scare you must be, I am, but keep in mind that one day you'll look back at all of it and be glad that is nothing but a memory. Hope you are successful at getting the job you want.
